{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-04",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Nightly backup job", "Database", "Backup files"],
    "dataStores": ["Database", "Cloud storage bucket"],
    "externalServices": ["Cloud storage provider"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["Database tier to cloud storage bucket", "Backup owners to reporting team"],
    "dataClasses": [],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Reporting team can read the entire database from unencrypted backup files",
      "scenario": "Anyone with access to the shared bucket, including every member of the reporting team and any contractor or service account added to that group, can download a nightly backup and open it directly because it is plaintext. A full database dump gives them every table and every row, far beyond the subset of data they are authorised to see for reporting, with no decryption step and no trace of what they read.",
      "component": "Cloud storage bucket holding nightly backups",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Database backups are written nightly to a cloud storage bucket. The backup files are not encrypted. The bucket is shared with the reporting team." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-312", "CWE-311"],
      "plainLanguage": "The nightly database copies are stored unlocked in a folder the reporting team can open, so they can read the whole database.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Encrypt database backups before they leave the database tier",
        "given": "a nightly database backup is produced",
        "when": "it is written to cloud storage",
        "then": "the backup is encrypted with a key that is not available to the reporting team or to any identity that only has bucket read access"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Sharing the backup bucket bypasses in-application access controls on the database",
      "scenario": "The reporting team is granted access to the bucket rather than to a filtered reporting dataset. A reporting user who could only query approved views in the application can instead restore a backup copy locally and query everything, including records of other teams and any restricted columns. Access granted for reporting becomes effectively database-administrator level read access, and adding a new member to the reporting group silently grants it.",
      "component": "Bucket access control / reporting team grant",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The bucket is shared with the reporting team." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-732", "CWE-285"],
      "plainLanguage": "Giving reporting access to the backup folder hands them a full copy of the database, skipping the limits the app normally puts on them.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Separate backup storage from reporting data access",
        "given": "the reporting team needs data for reports",
        "when": "access is provisioned",
        "then": "reporting identities have no read or list permission on the backup bucket and receive only the approved reporting dataset, with backup bucket access limited to the backup and restore roles"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "A backup file in the shared bucket can be altered so a restore reintroduces attacker-chosen data",
      "scenario": "If the shared bucket grant includes write or overwrite permission, or an attacker compromises any reporting account that has it, they can modify a plaintext backup file. Because the file is not encrypted or integrity-protected, there is no signature or checksum that would fail. The change surfaces during a disaster-recovery restore, when the altered rows, injected accounts or removed records are loaded straight into production and trusted.",
      "component": "Backup files in cloud storage",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The backup files are not encrypted. The bucket is shared with the reporting team." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-345", "CWE-353"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone who can write to the backup folder could edit a backup, and nobody would notice until it was restored into production.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Integrity-protect and write-protect stored backups",
        "given": "a backup file has been written to cloud storage",
        "when": "a restore is performed",
        "then": "the restore verifies a signature or checksum recorded at creation time and refuses to proceed on mismatch, and the bucket allows only append or immutable writes from the backup job with no overwrite rights for other principals"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Deleting objects in the shared bucket destroys the only recovery copy",
      "scenario": "A reporting user with delete rights, an account takeover, or ransomware on a workstation holding those credentials can delete or encrypt the nightly backups in the shared bucket. Since backups are written to this one bucket, the organisation loses its ability to recover the database after an outage or data-corruption incident, turning a recoverable failure into permanent data loss.",
      "component": "Cloud storage bucket holding nightly backups",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Database backups are written nightly to a cloud storage bucket." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-732"],
      "plainLanguage": "If someone deletes the files in the shared backup folder, there is nothing left to restore from.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Protect backups from deletion",
        "given": "nightly backups are stored in cloud storage",
        "when": "any principal other than the retention process attempts deletion or overwrite",
        "then": "the request is denied by object versioning or an immutability or retention lock, and at least one copy exists in a location no reporting identity can reach"
      }
    }
  ]
}
